title: The 3x+1 problem: new lower bounds on nontrivial cycle lengths
notes: Discrete Mathematics 118 (1993) 45-56. Wording from Lagarias's annotated bibliography (arXiv math/0309224, entry 53): any nontrivial cycle of T has period p = 301994 A + 17087915 B + 85137581 C with A, B, C nonnegative, B >= 1, and A C = 0, hence p >= 17087915; the method uses the continued fraction of log_2 3 and the truth of the conjecture for n < 2^40. The original was not read here. Reproduced by docs/problems/juggler_collatz_finance_mirror.md: Paper A's finance inequality with x_min in place of n log n gives the same minimum and the same lattice at 2^40, and 301994 alone is excluded because its bound 9.85e11 is just below 2^40. Paper A cites Eliahou as [13] for leftover packaging; the Lean EliahouLeftover of CycleFinanceLeftovers.lean is the Juggler-side form.
